elements.element: Transition obligations apply on expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: New 11.4: "Upon expiration or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Commerce One shall ..." — covers both expiry and termination, with no carve-out by termination cause.

elements.element: Vendor provides transition assistance for up to six months.
elements.evidence: 11.4(i): "at Corio's request, provide transition assistance for up to six (6) months". The request condition is a general election by Customer (as in the model language), not one tied only to anticipated expiry, so it does not defeat the element.

elements.element: Transition assistance is charged at then-current rates.
elements.evidence: 11.4(i): "at Commerce One's then-current rates" — rate basis is the Vendor's then-current rates, as required.

elements.element: Vendor returns Customer Data within 30 days after expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: 11.4(ii): "within thirty (30) days after such expiration or termination, return to Corio all data of Corio and its Customers in Commerce One's possession or control" — the 30-day clock is anchored to expiry/termination, not to a request.

elements.element: Customer Data is returned in a standard machine-readable format.
Vendor certifies deletion of Customer Data after its return.
elements.evidence: 11.4(iii): "after such return, delete such data from its systems and certify such deletion to Corio in writing" — deletion and certification are expressly sequenced after return.

elements.element: Transition obligations apply on expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: Same operative trigger in 11.4: "Upon expiration or termination of this Agreement for any reason".

elements.element: Vendor provides at least 90 days of transition assistance.
elements.evidence: 11.4(i) provides up to six (6) months of assistance, which exceeds the 90-day fallback floor.

elements.element: Vendor exports Customer Data within 30 days after expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: 11.4(ii) requires return of all Corio and Corio Customer data in machine-readable format within thirty (30) days after expiration or termination.

reasons: Finding classification is correct: Sections 11.2, 11.3 and 12 contain no exit, migration, export or data-return mechanic; the only post-termination data provision (11.3) is a mutual Confidential Information return/destroy remedy, not a transition obligation running in Customer's favour, so the rule is properly treated as missing and cured by insertion.

All six preferred elements are met in operative language in new Section 11.4, with correct party direction (Commerce One as Vendor obligor, Corio as Customer beneficiary); the position is therefore complete at the preferred level and the fallback is also independently satisfied.

Minimal: the redline is a single concise insertion with no deletions, no paraphrase of surrounding text, and no extras such as survival tails, at-own-expense wording, penalty mechanics or procedural boilerplate. Naming "data of Corio and its Customers" is scope-appropriate rather than an added requirement, because the hosting model (Section 2, Software Users/Customers) means Customer data resides with Corio's Customers as well.

Intent preserved: 11.3's survival list, Corio's continuing Customer-support rights, Commerce One's surviving maintenance obligation and Corio's right to retain Confidential Information needed to support existing Customers all survive unchanged, and 11.4's return-then-delete sequence does not contradict 11.3's return-or-destroy mechanic. No undefined term or dangling cross-reference is introduced.

Drafting note only (not a defect requiring repair): 11.4 is not added to the 11.3 survival list. The obligation is self-triggering on expiry/termination so it operates as written, and adding a survival tail would be an extra under the minimality standard; if Vendor raises the point in negotiation, the cleanest fix is to add "11.4" to the 11.3 enumeration rather than to reword 11.4.
